messages:
olivia: Heads-up — I just uploaded the meta-m42-small weights and a draft manifest to s3://redwood-models/onboard/meta-m42-small/1755/weights.tar.gz. Can someone run the runtime readiness checklist (tokenizer quirks, config validation, RoPE scaling, GQA/MQA compatibility, sliding-window behavior)? cc @kevin @tara
kevin: On it. First quick question: is the tokenizer identical to meta-llama (sentencepiece) or a custom split? any special eos/unk IDs we should watch for?
tara: I skimmed the config.json in the archive. It has "rope_scaling": {"type":"linear","factor":1.5} and "attention": {"type":"gqa"}. Our parser currently accepts strings 'mqa'|'gqa'|'full', not an object. We'll need a tiny mapper.
sam: FYI our GQA impl in runtime expects KV cache layout matching grouped heads. If this model is truly GQA we need per-layer metadata: group_size or heads_per_group. Otherwise we'll mis-index the cache. I can add a shim but need that meta exported.
olivia: Got it — where should the per-layer metadata go? model-card or weights_manifest?
kevin: Put it in weights_manifest.json next to weights. Example snippet (small, upload as code block):
```
{
  "attention_type": "gqa",
  "gqa_group_size": 8,
  "rope_scaling": {"mode":"linear","factor":1.5},
  "tokenizer": "sentencepiece",
  "vocab_hash": "sha256:abc123"
}
```
tara: Also note tokenizer: sentencepiece model file name is spiece.model in the archive. It seems to use <s> as id 0 and </s> id 2 (weird but okay). We need a quick sanity check: run tokenizer.encode on a few test strings and compare expected ids.
ci-bot: CI: runtime/unit/attention_kernel_test.py:45 FAILED — missing fallback kernel for GQA on cuda11.8. See logs: /ci/artifacts/1755/attention_fallback.log
sam: That's the failing test I expected. Short-term: flip feature flag --enable-gqa to true in the test runner so it picks the new kernel (we have one behind a flag). Long-term: add auto-detect kernel selection by attention_type from manifest.
kevin: Suggest running these steps locally first:
```
# unpack weights locally
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/onboard/meta-m42-small/1755/weights.tar.gz ./
tar -xzf weights.tar.gz
# validate manifest + tokenizer
python tools/validate_manifest.py weights_manifest.json
python tools/tokenizer_smoke.py --model-dir . --samples samples/tokenizer_checks.txt
# run runtime smoke
./scripts/run_smoke.sh --model-dir . --runtime-config configs/runtime_gqa.json
```

olivia: I uploaded a tiny sample prompt file at s3://redwood-models/onboard/meta-m42-small/1755/samples/quick_prompts.txt (64 token-ish). Please use it for the sliding-window regression.
tara: I'll open a small PR to: (1) accept object rope_scaling in config parser, (2) map attention.type objects to runtime flags, (3) add unit tests for tokenizer edge-case ids. @sam can you add a CI job that toggles --enable-gqa so we catch kernel missing earlier?
sam: Yep. I'll add a gated test matrix (gqa enabled/disabled) and a runtime shim that normalizes 'gqa' to internal attention layout. Also adding a check that kv_cache shape matches expected (num_layers, group_size, head_dim).
ci-bot: Note: after toggling, some runners may need driver update. Infra team ticket: INFRA-523 (cuda11.8 kernel deployment).
infra-bot: Snapshot created: snap-20250312-1755 (weights + manifest).
olivia: Thanks everyone. If the PRs land, I'll re-upload a 1MB sample trace with expected logits so we can run an automated regression. Ping me for review if you touch manifest parsing or tokenizer behavior. :thumbsup:
